data.title: Launch hivemind: publish npm package, register MCP, plugin marketplace

evidence: npx -y hivemind-agents@0.1.0 install worked from registry; package.json shows version 0.1.1; npm view shows name='hivemind-agents' version='0.1.1' dist-tags.latest='0.1.1'; curl to registry shows 'io.github.Leonhest/hivemind version 0.1.1 active'; docker shows 'hivemind installed' with hooks + MCP f

data.text: Future releases: stage the package with npm's stage publish command, then the maintainer (Leon) approves via passkey on npmjs.com. This avoids 2FA codes in chat or tokens in version control.
data.rationale: npm deprecated TOTP and token-bypass methods; passkey is the only option, and staged publishing is npm's workflow for it.

evidence: User ran `npm profile enable-2fa auth-and-writes` → 'Adding a new TOTP 2FA is no longer supported' 404; Leo then used `npx npm@latest stage publish` twice successfully; approval via iPhone passkey worked; PLAN.md documents this

data.spec: MCP server name in registry.modelcontextprotocol.io must be exactly `io.github.Leonhest/hivemind` (case-sensitive). Must also match mcpName field in package.json and server.json. Registry publish fails with 403 if name doesn't match account username case (`Leonhest` not `leonhest`).

evidence: mcp-publisher publish with lowercase name → 403 'You have permission to publish: io.github.Leonhest/*'; fixed by updating mcpName to 'io.github.Leonhest/hivemind' in package.json and server.json; v0.1.1 published successfully; curl to registry confirms 'io.github.Leonhest/hivemind'

evidence: Assistant message: 'What's left is optional: recording the demo GIF, testing Cursor live, testing GitLab, deleting the private hivemind-spike test repo'; hivedmind doctor shows Cursor hooks exist but 'only runs if Cursor is restarted to load them'

data.spec: Use `npx hivemind-agents <command>` or `~/.hivemind/bin/hivemind <command>` instead of plain `hivemind <command>`. Supported commands: status, doctor, plan, open.

evidence: `hivemind` isn't added to their PATH. So the README's `hivemind status` won't work as typed. They can use `npx hivemind-agents status` (or `doctor`, `plan`, `open`) or `~/.hivemind/bin/hivemind status` instead.
This is a small gap I can fix in the next release so plain `hivemind` works.
expect(execFileSync('hivemind', ['help'], { env, encoding: 'utf8' })).toContain('shared, live plan'); ... ✓ `hivemind` command: /Users/leonhesthaug/.hivemind/bin/hivemind

data.text: The shared plan (stored in git refs/hivemind/*) was pushed to GitHub and is now publicly readable on the public Leonhest/hivemind repo. It contains team decisions, task assignments, and member IDs. Proposal: (1) delete the ref `refs/hivemind/leon-hesthaug-e2d90a` from GitHub now, (2) make hivemind disable itself by default for public repos in v0.1.3 with `hivemind enable` to opt in. The check would use GitHub API via `gh` when available.

evidence: the shared plan is public too. The README says so, but nobody reading this would expect it. What I'd suggest: 1. Delete that ref from GitHub now... 2. Make hivemind turn itself off for public repos by default in the next release (0.1.3)

data.title: Privacy & security: public-repo notice, secret scrubbing, enable/disable

evidence: Version 0.1.3 published to npm, all tests pass: 'Tests 44 passed (44)', verified on public (Leonhest/hivemind) and private (hivemind-spike) repos.

data.spec: export function findRepo(cwd: string, opts: { includeDisabled?: boolean } = {}): Repo | null; When opts.includeDisabled is false (default), returns null if hivemind is disabled for that clone (via `hivemind disable`). When true, returns the Repo even if disabled (used internally for enable/disable commands).

evidence: findRepo signature updated: 'export function findRepo(cwd: string, opts: { includeDisabled?: boolean } = {}): Repo | null'

data.spec: export const isEnabled = (root: string) => tryGit(root, ['config', '--bool', 'hivemind.enabled']) !== 'false'; export function setEnabled(repo: Repo, enabled: boolean): void; export function githubSlug(remoteUrl: string): string | null; githubSlug returns 'owner/name' for GitHub remotes, else null.

evidence: New functions defined in git.ts: isEnabled, setEnabled, githubSlug with complete implementations.

data.spec: `hivemind disable` turns hivemind off for the current clone (stores in .git/config, kills daemon). `hivemind enable` turns it back on. Both print confirmation to stdout. `hivemind status` shows current visibility (PUBLIC, private, or no visibility info).

evidence: Case statements added: 'case 'disable': ... case 'enable': ... setEnabled(repo, enabled)'

data.spec: src/core/redact.ts applies regex patterns to every plan entry before write: (1) Private keys (PEM format). (2) API keys: sk-*, pk-*, rk-*, gh*, npm_, AKIA*, xox*. (3) JWTs (eyJ...). (4) Password/connection-string credentials: 'user:password@host' → 'user:[redacted]@host', 'password = value' → 'password = [redacted]. (5) Named fields: password, secret, api_key, access_token, auth_token, client_secret.

data.text: Visibility detection runs in background daemon (~1.5s max on first session, cached 24h). Prevents surprise public leaks.
data.rationale: Transparency: agents should know when their plan is publicly visible so they can make informed decisions about what to write.

evidence: Hook modified: 'await Promise.race([refreshVisibility(repo).catch(() => {}), new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1_500))])'; verified on Leonhest/hivemind (shows notice) and Leonhest/hivemind-spike (doesn't).
